text:
In the Court of Appeal of Alberta

Citation: R. v. Creaghan, 1991 ABCA 184

Date:
19910606

Docket:
12357

Registry:
Calgary

Between:

Her Majesty the Queen

Appellant

- and -

Jeremy Lawrence Creaghan and Kelly Scott Lyle

Respondents

The Court:

The Honourable Mr. Justice Shannon

The Honourable Mr. Justice Kerans

The Honourable Mr. Justice Irving

Memorandum of Judgment

COUNSEL:

B.Q.H. Der, for the Appellant

G. A. Tapp, for the Respondents

MEMORANDUM OF
JUDGMENT

KERANS, J.A.
(for the majority):

[
1
]

This is a Crown appeal from sentence on a charge
of wilful damage.

[
2
]

On two successive evenings, three young men, two
of whom are respondents on this appeal, sprayed crude and rude remarks
addressed to the Jewish people on the wall of a Calgary building. It cost about $1,000.00 to repair the damage. It is
obvious they thought that the building was a synagogue, but in fact it was the
World Faith Fellowship Church.

[
3
]

After a trial, the two respondents were
convicted and sentenced each to probation, with the two special conditions that
each pay $500.00 towards the damage caused and perform 200 hours of community
service. In addition, both were bound in custody over the noon break at the
trial so they could have a taste of incarceration.

[
4
]

The Crown appeals, and Mr. Der argued that the
racial prejudice of the accused was a major aggravating factor with the result
that a substantial period of incarceration was required. He relied heavily on
the decision of the Ontario Court of Appeal in
Lelas
(1991)
1990 CanLII 6836 (ON CA)
, 58 C.C.C.
(3d) 568, where a sentence was increased from six months to one year.

[
5
]

The Lelas case is distinguishable. Lelas was a
member of a racist organization who set out to upset the Jewish community and
succeeded. These two respondents have unremarkable backgrounds and no previous
involvement with the law. The third accused gave evidence at trial that it was
he who suggested this activity, and that the others were a little reluctant.
(The Crown could not say what has happened in his case.) The precise motive
here was not clear, and no inquiry in detail occurred because the accused were
not charged with promoting hatred.

[
6
]

That said, the obvious and disgusting racism in
the messages here is a major aggravating factor and the fit sentence for that
reason is a period of incarceration, albeit less than one year, or its
equivalent.

[
7
]

The real issue in the case, then, is whether 200
hours of community service is the equivalent of a sentence in the range
appropriate for this case. Despite the fact that 200 hours is a very high
number, the Crown says it is inadequate because neither the community nor other
potential offenders see them as the same.

[
8
]

In our view, there is much to be said for
community service over a short gaol sentence not in the name of leniency but in
the name of justice. Jails are expensive, and with short incarceration society
suffers again from the offence. And nobody sees the punishment. Community
service, by contrast, offers the community something in return for the offence
done, and it is a punishment that can be seen in the community.

[
9
]

It is said that community service will not deter
potential crime. We accept that racial assaults tend to be the behaviour of
unimaginative people who act out their own sense of inadequacy by jumping on
those whom they see as weaker or as the source of their problems. That being
the case, each case tends to breed emulation by others of that ilk. Deterrence
is an important sentencing factor. But we cannot gainsay the deterrent effect
of the prospect of having, as a punishment, to serve the victims, or others in
society who need help or have been victimized.

[
10
]

In Alberta, the form of community service is left to the administrators of the
program. In this case, however, we recommend that, if possible, the service be
performed for the Jewish community in Calgary.

[
11
]

We would dismiss the appeal.

DATED at CALGARY, Alberta

this 6th day of June,

A.D. 1991

SHANNON, J.
(dissenting):

[
12
]

During the evening of November 24th, 1989, one
Brett Hayes persuaded the respondent, Kelly Scott Lyle, to join him in spray
painting a building that had been a Jewish synagogue and which continued to
display Jewish symbols. They believed it to be a synagogue. They painted
swastikas, a Celtic cross and "S.S." on the door. Lyle painted the
slogan "A.R.M" skins on the building.

[
13
]

The following night they went there again
accompanied by the respondent, Jeremy Lawrence Creaghan. The following words
were painted on the edifice:

Hayes -             "Jews suck; Final solution N.F.; Eat shit
Jews; Burn in Hell Jews; K.K.K."

Lyle -                 "Die J.D.L. scum; White pride; S.S.; red
swastikas; God six million wasn't enough. Die J.D.L. Scum".

Creaghan -       "Nazi punks; Star of David sucks; Die Zionist
Pigs".

[
14
]

At the conclusion of their trial on a charge of
wilful damage, the learned trial judge found the respondents to be guilty and
suspended the passing of sentence. He placed them on probation for 2 years. The
terms of the probation order obliged each of them to pay $501.00 by way of
restitution and perform 200 hours of community service.

[
15
]

Those sentences were imposed because the respondents
are young, 19 and 20 years of age, and do not have criminal records. At the
outset, both of them expressed some reluctance to engage in such activities but
were persuaded to do so by Hayes. They are not members of an anti-semitic
organization.

[
16
]

The Crown appeals their sentences saying that
they are inadequate. I agree. The sentences imposed are probably sufficient to
deter the respondents, but they fail to provide the general deterrence required
to prevent others from engaging in such conduct. In addition, they fail to
express society's disapproval and denunciation of such reprehensible conduct,
aimed at insulting and terrorizing an important segment of our society - a
group that merits special protection because it has been the target of
vilification for centuries.

[
17
]

I would allow the Crown's appeal and impose a
sentence of imprisonment.

DATED at
CALGARY, Alberta

this 6th day of June,

A.D. 1991
